_comment: THE single source of truth for WHERE each analyzer package runs (issue #1801).
Every analyzer package in this repository is a Roslyn (or MSBuild) analyzer
that runs inside the compiler of EVERY project that references it. The cost
of that is not the number of findings: it is the number of ANALYZER CLASSES
the package registers times the number of COMPILATIONS the package is
referenced by. A rule set to `severity = none` is silenced; the analyzer
that implements it still runs. So the only lever that removes the cost is
the SCOPE, and a scope that is not written down drifts back to
solution-wide within a few months.
This file is that writing-down. The gate (tools/check-analyzer-scope.py)
fails when the tree says anything else, so the table and the tree cannot
drift apart. To widen or narrow a family: edit this file AND the props
files, and let the gate tell you whether the two agree.
HOW A SCOPE IS DECLARED IN THE TREE
* Every analyzer PackageReference carries the condition
Condition="'$(<property>)' != 'off'".
* The property is set to 'on' or 'off' by the scope file of the tree the
project lives in (src/, apps/, tests/), BEFORE that file imports the
repository-root Directory.Build.props.
* The repository-root file holds the DEFAULT, which is the scope of the
projects that import it and no other: samples/, tools/ and contrib/.
* A command-line -p:<property>=off wins over both, which is what the
measurement harness uses to turn exactly one family off.
HOW TO READ A ROW
id            the NuGet package id
property      the MSBuild property that switches it off
declared_in   the file(s) that carry the PackageReference element
scopes        the trees the package actually runs in
mode          'scope' = the scope properties decide;
'job'   = the package has its own switch and its own scope
(ReferenceTrimmer's scope is one CI step's switch, not the tree's)
reason        WHY the scope is what it is. A row without a reason is a
transcription, not a decision.

not_analyzers.reason: It ships the [Exposes]/[Injects] ATTRIBUTES, not an analyzer. It is a compile-time dependency of the composition roots under apps/ and it declares nothing the compiler has to check. It is listed here so that the gate's shape heuristic does not read it as an analyzer that arrived without a scope decision.

trees.root: the projects that import the repository-root Directory.Build.props and no other: samples/, tools/ and contrib/

families.reason: 284 RCS ids and no severity row for any of them, so every rule runs at the severity the package ships it with. It fires in product code, so it stays everywhere it can gate.

447 rule ids, of which 40 fire. MEASURED on this tree: 324 findings, and every one of them is under tests/ — src/, apps/, tools/ and samples/ produce none. #2030 measured the same split a month earlier. So this is the tree the family runs in; what the product tree gives up is written down in docs/ANALYZERS.md (the Analyzer scope section).
The base layer every other package is judged against: 329 CA ids. It is the SDK's own analyzer set, so removing it from a tree removes the CA rules from that tree rather than merely their findings.

Five rules, all at 'suggestion'. A suggestion is not promoted by TreatWarningsAsErrors, so this package cannot fail a build in ANY tree, and it produced no finding in any of them. It is kept where the shipped code is (src/, apps/) and dropped from the test tree and from the root scope.
46 rules, none of them about dynamic code (#1905). The nine rules that fire produce 41 findings, all under tests/, none of them a defect.

RS0030 over BannedSymbols.txt and BannedSymbols.DynamicCode.txt. NOT narrowed, and the reason is a coupling: tests/Harbor.Architecture.Tests/BannedApiProbe.cs runs the REAL analyzer in-process against a synthetic violation, and it finds the analyzer through the package path NuGet publishes for this package (the csproj's PackageReference Update + GeneratePathProperty). Narrowing the package out of the test tree would turn that Update into a no-op and move the control from 'the analyzer the build uses' to 'the newest version in the NuGet cache'. The family costs 5.2 s.
207 MA rows, each one configured with a reason. The package is the performance layer of the tree and it fires in product code.

37 DI ids; DI003, DI013, DI015, DI017 and DI019 are errors and they are the COMPOSITION ROOT's gate. The registrations live in src/Harbor.Hosting/Modules and the two apps/ roots, so this is where the family runs; a test project has no registration of its own to be wrong about.

CFE0001 is the mechanical guard for the ROP-001 crash class (a .Value on a failed Result<T>). NOT narrowed: the positive control (analyzers/CfeControl, deliberately outside tests/ and outside Harbor.slnx) inherits this root file and needs the analyzer there, and the family costs 0.2 s. The root props NoWarn the diagnostic under tests/ and samples/ anyway, so it produced nothing in the test tree either.

Not a Roslyn analyzer: it reads the MSBuild project files. Proj0037, Proj0040 and Proj0041 are errors and they are about the project files themselves, so they have to run wherever a project file is compiled.

29 rules, exactly one of them on (VSTHRD110, at 'suggestion'). The gate that decides 'is this an unobserved Task?' is HARCH003, a house analyzer, not this package (#1852). The test tree has its own async culture, so the package is not there.

It validates the [Exposes] attribute declarations, and only the composition roots under apps/ declare them. Its five rules are all at 'suggestion' because its flow analysis only follows the immediate method body; the real coverage is the DI registration tests.
The public-API freeze of #428, and it is a freeze of exactly two assemblies. The gate is compile-time: RS0016 and RS0017 are errors in the two frozen projects and exist in no other project.

The unused-reference detector. It is OFF by default and ON in exactly one place: the 'build' job's compile step, which sets the HarborReferenceTrimmer property. It runs there with its own codes demoted back to warnings (WarningsNotAsErrors), because its findings are warnings and this repository promotes warnings to errors. Since #2108 that compile is the lane's only compile of the tree; the job that used to compile it a second time is gone.
